Class GameController

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.it.GameController
All Implemented Interfaces:
GameEventListener
public class GameController extends Object implements GameEventListener
Game controller (Controller role in MVC).

In the client-server architecture, the server instantiates one GameController per game session (inside GameSession). Player actions arrive as messages over the network (socket or RMI), are forwarded here via handle(PlayerAction), and the resulting GameEvents are published to all registered listeners.

Two listeners are registered on the model:

  1. This controller — handles local view feedback (validation errors, logging).
  2. GameSession — serialises events and broadcasts them to connected clients.

The controller is deliberately thin:

  • It does not build actions itself (those come from the network layer).
  • It does not interpret events for remote clients (the network layer does that).
  • It validates, executes, and shows error feedback via the view if a local view is present (e.g. StubGameView on the server, or a real TUI/GUI in single-player mode).

  • Method Details

    • startGame

      public void startGame()
      Starts the game. Called once setup is complete and all players have joined.

    • handle

      public ValidationResult handle(PlayerAction action)
      Receives a player action (from the network layer or from a local view) and applies it to the model.

      Returns the validation outcome so the network layer can send an error message back to the client if the action was rejected.

      Parameters:
      action - the action sent by a player
      Returns:
      ValidationResult.Ok if applied; ValidationResult.Fail with a reason string if rejected

    • onEvent

      public void onEvent(GameEvent event)
      Forwards game events to the local view.

      In the full client-server setup, GameSession is registered as a second listener and handles broadcasting to remote clients. This method is responsible only for local display/logging.

      Specified by:
      onEvent in interface GameEventListener

    • getGame

      public Game getGame()
      Exposes the underlying game model. Intended for use by the server layer (e.g. GameSession) for reconnection and disconnection checks only — not for executing actions.
